query: What additive manufacturing strategy and post-processing route can enable the fabrication of a refractory high-entropy alloy family (Group IV-V transition metals) capable of retaining high-temperature structural integrity, and what specific microstructural state is hypothesized to optimize mechanical performance while mitigating the inherent brittleness associated with interstitial impurities?

generation.hypothesis: Fabrication of a Group IV-V refractory high-entropy alloy (e.g., NbMoTaWVCr) via Selective Laser Melting (SLM) with high linear energy density, followed by a post-processing route involving high-pressure torsion (HPT) or severe plastic deformation, will yield a nanostructured BCC matrix with a controlled volume fraction of fine, coherent Laves/oxide precipitates, thereby achieving high-temperature structural integrity by mitigating interstitial embrittlement through grain boundary strengthening and dislocation pinning.
generation.material_initial_state: NbMoTaWVCr powder with low oxygen content (<0.02 at.%) and nominal composition of Group IV-V transition metals, exhibiting a tendency to form brittle intermetallics (Laves, oxides) and suffer from interstitial embrittlement if not processed correctly.
generation.intervention: 1. Additive Manufacturing: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) with a linear energy density >= 2.83 J/mm to promote rapid solidification and single BCC solid solution formation. 2. Post-Processing: High-Pressure Torsion (HPT) or equivalent severe plastic deformation to refine grain size to the nanometer scale (<500 nm).
generation.conditions: Processing in an inert atmosphere (vacuum or argon) to minimize interstitial uptake; post-deformation annealing at temperatures sufficient to stabilize precipitates but below the solvus temperature to prevent grain coarsening.
generation.structural_mediator: A dual-phase microstructure consisting of a refined BCC solid solution matrix (grain size < 500 nm) containing a controlled volume fraction (approx. 7-10%) of fine, coherent Laves phase ((Cr,V)2(Ta,Nb)) and oxide phase (Ta2VO6) precipitates, alongside a reduced concentration of detrimental interstitial impurities (O, N) due to the initial low-oxygen powder and rapid solidification.
generation.mechanism: The high cooling rates of SLM suppress the formation of coarse brittle phases, favoring a supersaturated BCC solid solution. Subsequent severe plastic deformation (HPT) refines the grain size, increasing the density of grain boundaries which act as barriers to dislocation motion (Hall-Petch strengthening) and sinks for interstitial impurities, thereby mitigating the inherent brittleness associated with interstitials. The fine precipitates provide additional precipitation hardening and pin dislocations, enhancing high-temperature stability.
generation.predicted_outcome: The resulting alloy will exhibit a yield strength > 3400 MPa and plasticity > 5% at room temperature, with retained high-temperature structural integrity (resistance to creep and oxidation) due to the stable nanostructure and protective oxide film formation, overcoming the brittleness typically seen in cast RHEAs with interstitials.
generation.baseline: Conventional arc-melted or cast NbMoTaWVCr alloys which typically exhibit coarse grains, high volume fractions of brittle Laves and oxide phases (>10%), and significant interstitial embrittlement leading to low ductility (<2%) and poor high-temperature performance.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies specifically to Group IV-V transition metal RHEAs (Nb, Mo, Ta, W, V, Cr) processed via SLM and HPT; it may not hold for alloys with significantly higher Al/Si content which form brittle silicides/B2 phases, or for processing routes that do not achieve the necessary cooling rates or grain refinement.
generation.uncertainty: While SLM has been shown to form single BCC solutions in NbMoTaW (PMC6427779) and high strength in NbMoTaWVCr with specific phase fractions (PMC7866258), the specific combination of SLM followed by HPT to achieve <500 nm grains in this specific multi-component system has not been explicitly demonstrated in the provided evidence. The exact optimal energy density and deformation parameters for the VCr-containing system remain to be experimentally verified.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate NbMoTaWVCr samples using SLM at linear energy densities below 2.83 J/mm and without subsequent HPT treatment. Compare these against samples processed with >= 2.83 J/mm followed by HPT. Additionally, intentionally introduce 2.0 at.% Oxygen/Nitrogen to the powder prior to SLM to test the mitigation hypothesis.
measurements: Phase fraction and morphology of Laves/oxide phases via XRD/SEM
Room temperature yield strength and elongation via uniaxial compression
Interstitial concentration (O, N) via inert gas fusion analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if: (1) SLM samples without HPT show no significant grain refinement (<500 nm) or strength increase compared to cast counterparts; (2) Samples with intentional high interstitial content (>0.5 at.%) fail to show improved ductility or strength compared to low-interstitial controls; or (3) The combination of SLM and HPT results in the formation of coarse, brittle intermetallic networks rather than fine precipitates, leading to catastrophic failure at low strains.
